text:
A **200 W panel** is a practical choice for a 1,000 Wh station. It recharges the station in about 1.5 days of good sun. For a full recharge in a single day, you need roughly **300 to 350 W** of panel in summer-like conditions.

**Why the number varies**

Sources assume different amounts of sun and different system losses:

- **Rule of thumb:** Divide the battery's watt-hours by five. That gives 200 W for 1,000 Wh, which recharges the station in about a day and a half of decent sun. [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)
- **At 4.5 peak sun hours:** A 200 W panel delivers about 630 Wh per day, so a 1,000 Wh station refills in a little over 1.5 days. [Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)
- **One-day refill, by sun hours** (panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75)):
  - 3 hours: about 450 W
  - 4 hours: about 340 W
  - 5 hours: about 270 W
  - 6 hours: about 230 W

  [Power Station Runtime Calculator](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)
- **Seasonal extremes:** About 300 W works in a good summer. In a northern January (about 2 peak sun hours), you'd need roughly 735 W. [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)

**Check the station's solar input limit**

Panels beyond the station's maximum solar input add nothing, so a 400 W panel won't charge a station capped at 200 W any faster. Also confirm that the panel's open-circuit voltage falls within the station's input voltage range. [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)

**Example panel:** The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is a common option. Its 45.3 V open-circuit voltage suits many 12–60 V inputs, but it weighs 18.5 kg. This review page earns a commission if you buy through its link. Verify the price and any discount code at checkout.
